title: Deterministic Output Stripping
summary: Extract and validate an explicit public output contract so model responses cannot leak internal fields, malformed wrappers, or unintended executable content.
overview: Deterministic output stripping removes material outside an explicitly permitted response representation. Examples include extracting a schema-valid object from a designated channel, dropping internal metadata fields, and rendering only approved display fields. The safest architecture defines the output contract before generation and rejects ambiguity rather than heuristically deleting suspicious fragments afterward.

Stripping is not a substitute for content safety, authorization, or factual validation. A perfectly shaped JSON object can still contain disallowed data or unsupported claims. Avoid relying on text markers to separate private reasoning from public answers; use supported structured channels and a strict allowlist of fields suitable for the recipient.

production.poc: A prototype may remove Markdown fences around a known JSON response. Test embedded fences and malformed responses before assuming this is a reliable parser.
production.production: Production uses a formal schema, strict parsing, field allowlists, size limits, and explicit refusal or error handling. Do not silently repair semantically ambiguous output.
production.scale: At scale, version response contracts and monitor rejection by model and prompt version. Keep raw diagnostic payloads access-controlled while exposing only the normalized public artifact to clients and search indexes.

components.name: Output contract
components.role: Defines required public fields, types, bounds, and allowed nested structures.

components.name: Strict parser
components.role: Parses the expected representation without evaluating code or accepting trailing ambiguous content.

components.name: Field allowlist
components.role: Removes internal metadata and blocks unrecognized fields from the public response.

components.name: Semantic validator
components.role: Checks business values, evidence references, and recipient authorization after structural validation.

components.name: Renderer
components.role: Escapes display content and serializes only the approved public representation.

flow.title: Declare response shape
flow.description: Specify public fields, required evidence, error variants, and maximum payload size before generation.

flow.title: Receive typed output
flow.description: Prefer a supported structured response channel and preserve its completion status.

flow.title: Parse strictly
flow.description: Reject malformed, truncated, multiply encoded, or ambiguous payloads without executing them.

flow.title: Apply allowlist
flow.description: Select approved fields and discard internal diagnostics using schema-aware transformations.

flow.title: Validate meaning
flow.description: Check identifiers, factual support, and data permissions separately from syntax.

flow.title: Render safely
flow.description: Escape content for its destination and expose a clear retryable error when validation fails.

diagrams.caption: The publication boundary validates structure and meaning before rendering only permitted fields.

useCase.title: Publishing invoice exception summaries
useCase.situation: An accounts-payable platform generates structured exception summaries for staff and exposes a limited status view to suppliers.
useCase.problem: Raw model output sometimes includes explanatory wrappers, internal risk notes, or fields intended only for the operations team.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must produce stable machine-readable results and publish only the fields authorized for each audience.
useCase.architecture: A typed response contract separates internal analysis artifacts from a public exception object, followed by schema validation and audience-specific allowlists.
runtime: The model returns an exception code, supported explanation, and evidence references; the parser rejects unexpected wrappers or missing fields.
The supplier renderer receives only approved status and requested-document fields, while staff access the separately protected internal artifact.
useCase.failure: If a response is truncated, the system returns a validation error and preserves the prior valid status instead of publishing a partial object.
useCase.impact: Measure parse rejection, unauthorized-field attempts, schema drift, and client rendering failures. A low parser-error rate does not establish factual correctness.

tradeoffs.cost: Some otherwise useful responses require regeneration or review.

tradeoffs.benefit: Internal fields cannot leak through accidental serialization.
tradeoffs.cost: New public fields need deliberate contract changes.

tradeoffs.benefit: Known harmless wrappers can be handled consistently.
tradeoffs.cost: Excessive repair logic can conceal model regressions.

failures.scenario: Internal metadata appears in a nested object
failures.detection: Recursive schema validation identifies unapproved fields.
failures.recovery: Reject or remove them according to the explicit contract and log the event.

failures.detection: Renderer treats it as data and escapes it.
failures.recovery: Preserve the literal value without executing or interpreting markup.

mistakes.mistake: Using regular expressions as a general JSON parser
mistakes.fix: Parse with a strict format-aware library.
Validate nested structures and enforce recursive allowlists.

mistakes.mistake: Calling valid syntax a safe answer
mistakes.fix: Apply evidence, policy, and destination-specific rendering checks.

whenToUse: Model output feeds APIs, interfaces, or downstream automation.
Different recipients require different public field sets.
A stable schema can define acceptable publication.
whenNotToUse: The requirement is unrestricted raw model transcript export.
Output meaning cannot be validated where correctness is essential.
Heuristic stripping would silently alter consequential values.
checklist: Define public and internal schemas separately.
Handle refusal and error variants explicitly.
Escape content for the rendering destination.
Track schema rejection by model version.
